title: Ambani Adds $6.3 Billion in a Day as Reliance Shares Jump 11.6% on Record Quarterly Profit
excerpt: Reliance's best trading session in over six years, driven by a 40.6% rise in September-quarter profit, made Mukesh Ambani the world's biggest gainer on Forbes' real-time rich list and kept him India's richest person.
body:
• Mukesh Ambani added $6.3 billion to his fortune on Monday, the biggest one-day gain on Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires list, taking his net worth to $88.8 billion.
  • Reliance Industries shares jumped 11.6% to close at Rs 1,300, their strongest session in more than six years, after September-quarter results beat expectations.
  • Reliance's profit attributable to shareholders rose 40.6% year on year to Rs 25,548 crore, on revenue up 27.8% to Rs 3.62 lakh crore.
  • Forbes now ranks Ambani 23rd in the world and India's richest person, ahead of Gautam Adani at 26th with $79.12 billion.

Mukesh Ambani was the world's biggest billionaire gainer on Monday, adding $6.3 billion, or 7.85%, to his fortune in a single session, according to Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires list, as Reliance Industries shares surged after a stronger-than-expected September quarter. The gain lifted Ambani's net worth to $88.8 billion and to 23rd place globally, keeping him India's richest person ahead of Gautam Adani, whom Forbes ranked 26th with $79.12 billion. The second-biggest gainer on the list, Spanish retail billionaire Amancio Ortega, added $1.7 billion.

The earnings behind the rally

Reliance shares closed at Rs 1,300 on the National Stock Exchange, up 11.6% on the day and at their session high, in the stock's strongest trading day in more than six years. The stock was the biggest gainer on the Nifty 50. The rally added Rs 1,83,298 crore to the company's market value, taking it to Rs 17,57,877 crore.

The trigger was the September quarter, the second quarter of fiscal 2027. Reliance reported consolidated net profit attributable to shareholders of Rs 25,548 crore, up 40.6% from a year earlier and ahead of analyst expectations, with total profit after tax of Rs 29,550 crore described as a record for the company. Consolidated revenue rose 27.8% to Rs 3.62 lakh crore, and earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization climbed 23.9% to a record Rs 62,409 crore. The refining business's core earnings surged 68%, while Jio Platforms' core earnings rose 16.6%.

Why one stock moves one fortune so far

Ambani's family controls Reliance through the promoter group, which holds roughly half the company. That concentration means a double-digit move in the share price translates mechanically into billions of dollars of paper wealth in a day, in either direction. Monday's move also follows the October listing of Jio Platforms, which reached a market capitalization of $137 billion on listing, making it India's second most valuable company after its parent, according to Forbes' profile of Ambani.

What it means for investors

For holders of Reliance, the quarter, not the rich list, is the story: a refining-led beat, record group profit, and a newly listed telecom asset now carrying its own market value. Forbes' real-time ranking will keep moving with the share price. Readers tracking the stock can follow the figures on Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires list as reported by YourStory, and should treat single-day wealth swings as a mark-to-market reading, not cash earned.
